newsitem.title: TURKEY: IMF group head says no Turkey stand-by request.
newsitem.headline: IMF group head says no Turkey stand-by request.

text.p: The head of an International Monetary Fund delegation visiting Ankara said on Monday the Turkish government had made no request for a stand-by agreement with the IMF.
But delegation head Martin Hardy said after meeting State Minister Abdullah Gul that the organisation would be open to such a request.
"It is not something we are discussing at this point but in due course if that were to be the request of the government there's no reason in principle why not," he told reporters.

Financial analysts believe the discipline of an accord would help the country to address long-standing problems of high inflation, currently running at around 80 percent annually, and shaky public finances.
Hardy stressed the importance for Turkey of trying to balance the budget, which in 1996 showed a deficit of 1,217 trillion lira.
"It certainly should be the aim, strong aim of the government to maintain very strict discipline of expenditure and seek to balance the budget as rapidly as possible," he said.
Hardy is due to meet Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller on Wednesday or Thursday at the end of two weeks' talks in Turkey.
